target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures describe the hardware foundation of the accelerated computing platform. D020 identifies GPUs as the foundation, available in industry servers and DGX supercomputers, with reference designs (HGX, EGX, etc.). D018 identifies GPUs as the foundation for parallel workloads, available in industry standard servers, and notes the platform's expansion to include DPUs and CPUs. The core subject is the composition of the hardware platform foundation (GPUs primarily, with specific system implementations).

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose a data center portfolio foundation built on multiple accelerators (CPUs, GPUs, DPUs) to optimize diverse workloads. NVDA frames this as an expansion of its platform to include CPUs in FY2024 to optimize the 'computing, networking and storage stack.' AMD similarly describes its Data Center segment as including server-class CPUs, GPUs, and DPUs, leveraging these combinations to 'enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.'

sentences.text: Beyond GPUs, our data center platform expanded to include DPUs in fiscal year 2022 and CPUs in fiscal year 2024.
We can optimize across the entire computing, networking and storage stack to deliver data center-scale computing solutions.
The Data Center segment primarily includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: While NVDA provides a broad accelerated computing platform including custom logic via its own hardware, AVGO focuses specifically on providing the IP and technology platforms that allow customers to design their own custom ASICs for AI and high-performance computing. NVDA optimizes the 'entire... stack' with its own GPUs, DPUs, and CPUs, whereas AVGO enables customers to 'design and develop application specific integrated circuits (ASICs)' that integrate 'embedded logic... and processor cores' to meet similar AI and HPC targets.

sentences.text: We can optimize across the entire computing, networking and storage stack to deliver data center-scale computing solutions.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and INTC describe a multi-architecture hardware strategy for the data center. NVDA’s platform is founded on GPUs but expanded to include DPUs and CPUs to address various workload types. Similarly, INTC describes an 'xPU approach' beyond CPUs, encompassing GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to 'address diverse workloads' and meet 'diverse computing needs' by offering leading products across different architectural categories.

sentences.text: Beyond GPUs, our data center platform expanded to include DPUs in fiscal year 2022 and CPUs in fiscal year 2024.
At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.
Beyond the CPU, we deliver a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and MU both address the specific demands of AI workloads in the data center, but from different layers of the stack. NVDA focuses on the compute foundation (GPUs) for AI training and inferencing, while MU focuses on the high-performance storage layer required for AI data lakes and computing workloads. NVDA provides the 'accelerated computing platform' for parallel workloads, whereas MU provides 'high performance storage' with SSDs featuring 'high performance, reliability, and endurance for AI data lake applications.'

sentences.text: At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.
Our 6500 30TB SSDs features high performance, reliability, and endurance for AI data lake applications.
In 2024, we began sampling our 9550 series SSD to meet the growing demands of AI, high-performance computing, and many other workloads.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and QCOM utilize System-on-Chip (SoC) or heterogeneous computing architectures that combine CPUs and GPUs (and NPUs) to handle specific workload types efficiently. However, the target market and scale differ significantly. NVDA’s platform is designed for 'data center-scale computing solutions' and 'parallel workloads such as... training and inferencing of neural networks.' In contrast, QCOM’s SoC architecture is designed for 'high-performance and low-power computing' in client devices (PCs, smartphones) and includes an 'AI Engine' for 'on-device' inference, highlighting a divergence in compute scale and power profile compared to NVDA's data center focus.

sentences.text: We can optimize across the entire computing, networking and storage stack to deliver data center-scale computing solutions.
At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.

We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.
